statement: Let t, r ≥ 1 be integers. For each 1 ≤ i ≤ t, let Xi and Mi be nonempty finite sets with uniform probability, and let Yi be a specified copy of (F2)a, where a ≥ 1 and L = 2a. For m ∈ Mi and y ∈ Yi, let πm i,y be a probability distribution on Xi. Suppose that, for some θ ≥ 0, these distributions satisfy Em∈Mi πm i,y(x) = 1 |Xi| (x ∈ Xi, y ∈ Yi) (4.1) and, for every real function g : Xi → R and every y ∈ Yi, Em∈Mi   X x∈Xi πm i,y(x)g(x) − Ex∈Xi g(x)   2 ≤ θEx∈Xi g(x)2 . (4.2) Let F : Q i Xi → Sr + satisfy tr F(x) ≤ B for all x, where B > 0 and Sr + is the cone of real symmetric positive semidefinite r-by-r matrices. Fix λ > 1 such that Lλ2 CLθ ≤ 1, (4.3) where CL = 2L−1 is the constant of Lemma 3.1. For m = (m1, . . . , mt) ∈ Q i Mi, define Fm(y) = X x∈ Q i Xi t Y i=1 πmi i,yi (xi) ! F(x). (4.4) There is a finite integer R and a family of functions Hm q : Q i Yi → RR×r, indexed by m ∈ Q i Mi and q ∈ Λt, such that Fm(y) = X q∈Λt Hm q (y)T Hm q (y). (4.5) For each m, q, form the horizontal concatenation and its Gram matrix Um q = h λdist(q,p)/2 b Hm q,p i p∈Λt , Cm q = Um q (Um q )T , (4.6) where b Hm q,p is the Fourier coefficient of Hm q at p. The family can be chosen so that, for independent uniform mi, Em X q∈Λt Cm q 2 F ≤ 2t B2 . (4.7) Consequently, at least one m satisfies X q,p∈Λt λdist(q,p) b Hm q,p 2 F ≤ Lt√ r B 2t/2 . (4.8)
